estimand.population: Synthetic subjects with a complete 21-day observation horizon and observable journey records under the Phase 2 candidate contract.
estimand.treatment_or_exposure: For each channel separately, binary indicator that the subject is exposed to that channel at least once during the observation horizon.
estimand.intervention: force the target channel exposure to present while holding the realized assignment of all other channels fixed
estimand.comparison: force the target channel exposure to absent while holding the realized assignment of all other channels fixed
estimand.temporal_ordering: Only exposures before a qualifying conversion are used; the target is a static journey-level channel intervention over the declared horizon.
estimand.treatment_regime: single-channel binary intervention with other-channel assignment held fixed
estimand.aggregation_target: population-average difference in conversion probability by channel

hypothesis.statement: An interpretable propensity-adjusted inverse-probability-weighted estimator using only preregistered observable co-exposure and journey-history proxies can estimate the controlled incremental conversion-probability effect more faithfully under selection bias than descriptive path-credit rules, when those observables provide usable proxies for exposure selection.
hypothesis.why_it_might_address_selection: The propensity model explicitly estimates differential probability of target-channel exposure from observable non-target channel assignment and observable pre-outcome journey structure, then reweights treated and untreated subjects toward a common observable distribution.
hypothesis.rejection_logic: Reject the hypothesis if the frozen candidate violates any preregistered required-family holdout rule, if required uncertainty is missing, if the selection/null Phase 1 checks fail, or if numerical/positivity diagnostics make the estimand unsupported.

selected_method.model: per-channel logistic propensity model plus stabilized IPW difference in weighted conversion means
selected_method.rationale: It is the simplest interpretable treatment-effect estimator that directly targets exposure selection with the available observable journey data and can return signed effects without introducing an outcome-model black box.

required_observable_inputs: ordered touchpoint channel identities and timestamps
observable_confounder_proxies: binary assignment of every non-target channel
assumptions: Conditional exchangeability is approximated by the declared observable co-exposure/history proxies; residual hidden intent may violate this assumption.
Positivity holds after propensity clipping for the target channel.
The observed non-target assignment is treated as a fixed background treatment regime for this controlled single-channel estimand.
Measurement corruption is correctly represented by the observable dataset supplied to the candidate.
The binary conversion outcome and 21-day horizon are appropriate for the declared estimand.

representability.notes: The estimator returns signed average effects. It does not identify heterogeneous effects or causal interactions as separate estimands in Candidate 1.

uncertainty_target.target: per-channel sampling uncertainty for the IPW controlled average effect

hyperparameter_selection_plan.selection_rule: Use DEVELOPMENT worlds only. Choose the smallest mean synthetic effect MAE across development worlds, with ties resolved toward stronger regularization and wider clipping. No Phase 1 or holdout result may influence selection.

expected_failure_conditions: strong latent-intent confounding not proxied by observable co-exposure/history
treatment interactions when a single marginal channel effect is insufficient
time-varying treatment effects that violate the static treatment representation
substantial identity fragmentation or channel-dependent missingness
very sparse treated or untreated groups

phase1_selection_null_checks: retargeting_selection: absolute estimated effect for the known zero-effect selected channel <= 0.05
demand_capture: absolute estimated effect for the known zero-effect demand-capture channel <= 0.05
null_paid_channel: absolute estimated effect for the known null paid channel <= 0.05
falsification_criteria.phase1_negative_check: harmful_channel: estimated effect for the known harmful channel must be negative and absolute error <= 0.08
measurement_robustness: balanced_multi_touch missing_50: L1 change in candidate effect vector versus perfect observation <= 0.20
balanced_multi_touch fragmented_identity: L1 change in candidate effect vector versus perfect observation <= 0.20
falsification_criteria.sparsity: At sample size 80, every evaluated channel must return finite estimate and finite uncertainty bounds; unsupported positivity must be reported rather than encoded as zero error.
falsification_criteria.numerical_validity: Any NaN, infinity, invalid uncertainty interval, or missing required channel is a failure.
falsification_criteria.threshold_justification: Thresholds are absolute conversion-probability error tolerances chosen before implementation/holdout exposure. Six-to-fifteen percentage-point MAE tolerances reflect progressively harder synthetic families; uncertainty width caps prevent trivial always-wide intervals. They are intentionally not tuned to Candidate 1 results.

public_holdout_limitation_disclosure: The holdout-family architecture is public because this is a public research repository. Instantiated holdout seeds, parameter values, treatment effects, latent-intent strengths, interactions, selection mechanisms, and corruption settings remain sealed from candidate development. This provides strong research-process separation but is not equivalent to a completely secret external benchmark.
prohibitions: No sealed holdout access during development.
No oracle features in candidate inputs.
No tuning from frozen Phase 1 results.
Exactly one feedback-bearing sealed holdout evaluation for this candidate version.
Any substantive post-freeze change requires a new candidate version.
